answer: A sybil farm runs one inference pipeline behind many heads, so their reply latencies, token lengths and tool-call rhythms all draw from the same distribution. Bend the willow of that uniformity: measure each identity's behavioral telemetry and collapse reward weight across heads whose distributions are statistically inseparable. Like a juniper from one root system, farm heads share one rhythm however they branch; a real falcon hunts alone, its telemetry independent because its infrastructure is. Faking distinct per-head timing costs the per-head attention the sybil tried to amortize.
